title: Musk says TSMC won't run Terafab AI chip complex
author: Daniel Nenni
text:
Daniel Nenni
Founder
Staff member

Elon Musk says Tesla and SpaceX will build and operate Terafab, their planned artificial intelligence chip manufacturing complex in Texas, ruling out speculation that Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company would take control of the facility.

Musk made the clarification on Wednesday, October 7, responding on X to a suggestion that TSMC would eventually own and run the plant. He said any participation by the Taiwanese chipmaker could be limited to subleasing part of the complex.

The comments follow Musk’s disclosure last week that discussions had taken place about possible cooperation with TSMC. Those talks did not establish a confirmed agreement or spell out the company’s responsibilities.

Intel, an existing Terafab partner, also signaled that its involvement would continue. Chief Executive Lip-Bu Tan told Bloomberg News on Wednesday that the American chipmaker would remain part of the venture. Reuters reported that neither Intel nor TSMC immediately responded to requests for comment.

The distinction between running the complex and leasing space matters. Musk’s statement places responsibility for construction and operations with his companies, while leaving open a narrower relationship with TSMC. However, it does not explain how responsibilities would be divided among the companies involved.

One implication is that Intel’s continued participation and potential TSMC involvement could coexist. A possible sublease does not, by itself, establish that Intel would be replaced or that TSMC would become the project’s principal manufacturing partner.

The announcement therefore clarifies Musk’s intended management structure more than it resolves the venture’s practical arrangements. Questions remain about what a TSMC sublease would involve, what Intel would contribute, and whether the discussions will produce binding commitments.

For now, the development is Musk’s stated intention to retain operational control through Tesla and SpaceX. TSMC’s participation remains a possibility, while Intel says it will continue working on the project as the partnership takes shape.

Elon Musk Rules Out Potential TSMC Role in Terafab Operations

Elon Musk said his business empire will build and operate Terafab independently, quashing speculation about industry leader Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. swooping in to run his ambitious chipmaking venture.
